# Import Data
```{r}
# Get list of all CSV files in the 'csv_file' folder
csv_files <- list.files(path = "csv_file", pattern = "*.csv", full.names = TRUE)

# Extract file names without extension to use as dataframe names
df_names <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(csv_files))

# Read CSV files and assign each to a separate dataframe in the global environment
for(i in seq_along(csv_files)) {
  assign(df_names[i], read.csv(csv_files[i]))
}
```

# Check the marks achieved and number of steps taken by individual students
```{r}
# Create the processing function
process_dataframe <- function(df, df_name) {
  summary_data <- df %>%
    # Filter out NA ids
    filter(!is.na(id)) %>%
    # Group by id and summarize
    group_by(id) %>%
    summarise(
      max_step = if(all(is.na(step))) NA else max(step, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_marks = if(all(is.na(marks))) NA else max(marks, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    # Calculate overall maximums
    filter(max_marks > 0) %>% 
    summarise(
      mean_step = round(mean(max_step, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
      mean_marks = round(mean(max_marks, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      max_marks = max(max_marks, na.rm = TRUE),
      n = n()
    ) %>%
    # Add dataframe name
    mutate(dataframe = df_name) %>%
    # Reorder columns to match desired output
    select(dataframe, mean_step, mean_marks, max_marks, n)
  
  return(summary_data)
}

# Create empty list to store results
all_summaries <- list()

# Process each dataframe
for(df_name in df_names) {
  # Get the dataframe from its name using get()
  current_df <- get(df_name)
  # Process it and store result
  all_summaries[[df_name]] <- process_dataframe(current_df, df_name)
}

# Combine all results into one dataframe
final_summary <- bind_rows(all_summaries)
write_csv(final_summary, "individual_questions_steps_and_scores.csv")
```

```{r}
# First, let's process the data to get max steps per ID
summarized_steps <- `df_data_L09_Sorting_(Advance)_Q2` %>%
  filter(!is.na(id)) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(max_step = max(step, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_edit_distance = mean(edit_distance, na.rm = TRUE),
            marks = max(marks, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  filter(marks > 0)

# Create the dotplot
ggplot(summarized_steps, aes(x = max_step)) +
  geom_dotplot(binwidth = 1, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5,
               stackratio = 1.5,
               dotsize=1) +
  labs(
    #title = "Total number of steps taken by individual students. Each dot represents one student",
    x = "Total Number of Steps",
    y = "Count"
  ) 
ggsave("total_steps_sorting_q2.png")

# Calculate correlation
cor_value <- cor(summarized_steps$max_step, summarized_steps$mean_edit_distance, 
                method = "pearson")

# Create the scatterplot with correlation annotation
ggplot(summarized_steps, aes(x = max_step, y = mean_edit_distance)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE, alpha = 0.2) +
  annotate("text", x = max(summarized_steps$max_step), y = max(summarized_steps$mean_edit_distance),
           label = sprintf("r = %.2f", cor_value),
           hjust = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Total Number of Steps",
    y = "Mean Edit Distance"
  ) +
  ylim(0, max(summarized_steps$mean_edit_distance)) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave("total_steps_vs_edit_distance_sorting_q2.png")
```
```{r}
# Create a function to generate and save plots for each dataframe
analyze_and_plot_dataframe <- function(df, df_name) {
  # Process data
  summarized_steps <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(id)) %>%
    group_by(id) %>%
    summarise(max_step = max(step, na.rm = TRUE),
              mean_edit_distance = mean(edit_distance, na.rm = TRUE),
              marks = max(marks, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    filter(marks > 0)
  
  # Calculate all correlations
  cor_step_edit <- cor(summarized_steps$max_step, summarized_steps$mean_edit_distance, 
                      method = "pearson", use = "complete.obs")
  cor_edit_marks <- cor(summarized_steps$mean_edit_distance, summarized_steps$marks,
                       method = "pearson", use = "complete.obs")
  cor_step_marks <- cor(summarized_steps$max_step, summarized_steps$marks,
                       method = "pearson", use = "complete.obs")
  
  # Create and save dotplot
  p1 <- ggplot(summarized_steps, aes(x = max_step)) +
    geom_dotplot(binwidth = 1, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5,
                 stackratio = 1.5,
                 dotsize = 1) +
    labs(
      x = "Total Number of Steps",
      y = "Count"
    )
  
  ggsave(paste0("total_steps_", df_name, ".png"), p1)
  
  # Create and save scatterplot for steps vs edit distance
  p2 <- ggplot(summarized_steps, aes(x = max_step, y = mean_edit_distance)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue", size = 3) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE, alpha = 0.2) +
    annotate("text", x = max(summarized_steps$max_step), 
             y = max(summarized_steps$mean_edit_distance),
             label = sprintf("r = %.2f", cor_step_edit),
             hjust = 1) +
    labs(
      x = "Total Number of Steps",
      y = "Mean Edit Distance"
    ) +
    ylim(0, max(summarized_steps$mean_edit_distance)) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  ggsave(paste0("total_steps_vs_edit_distance_", df_name, ".png"), p2)
  
  # Return all correlations
  return(data.frame(
    dataframe = df_name,
    cor_step_edit = cor_step_edit,
    cor_edit_marks = cor_edit_marks,
    cor_step_marks = cor_step_marks
  ))
}

# Apply function to all dataframes
correlations <- lapply(df_names, function(name) {
  df <- get(name)
  analyze_and_plot_dataframe(df, gsub("df_data_", "", name))
}) %>% bind_rows()

# View correlations for all dataframes
print(correlations)

write_csv(correlations, "cor_step_edit.csv")
```
